surface_mechanism_description: The surface reaction mechanism involves the use of different precursors (Mn(thd)3, La(thd)3, Ca(thd)2, and ozone) in an alternating pulsing sequence. The growth rate and stoichiometry are influenced by the surface utilization of each precursor, where the surface area coverage of each precursor affects the deposition of the respective metal components. The Mn(thd)3 precursor decomposes at around 240 uC, but its stability increases when used with Ca and La, allowing ALD growth up to 335 uC. The decomposition of Mn(thd)3 leads to the release of ligands that can be captured by Ca and La species on the surface, facilitating self-controlled growth.
intermediate_species: Ca and La species on the surface
evidence: The text discusses the decomposition of Mn(thd)3 at around 240 uC, where Mn(thd)x (x = 1 or 2) fragments lose ligands and new active sites become available. It also mentions that thd ligands freed from the adsorbed Mn(thd)x fragment can be captured by Ca and/or La species on the growing surface. The mechanism is further supported by the observation that the growth rate of MnOx films is reduced when small amounts of La or Ca are introduced, indicating the involvement of these species in the surface reactions.
